text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government study shows that 10,000 state employees could be pensioned off, saving government spending of 23 million dinars ($32 million) a year. Study finds that ministries and government bodies employ 134,000 people, two thirds of them at the ministries of education and health.
- Government source tells Al-Rai parliamentary elections will be held on November 8 but Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed says no date has yet been fixed.
- Six nationalist parties complete merger process; two more will join them soon.
- Official figures show Jordan registered a 1996 trade deficit of two billion dinars, with exports at 1.04 billion and imports at 3.04 billion.
- Planning Minister Rima Khalaf says elements of social safety net to be worked out on Sunday before a tour of foreign donor countries.
- Former information minister Marwan Muasher nominated as Jordan's ambassador to United States.
